messages:
maria: quick heads-up — during the long-context perf run (12k tokens) the KV cache resident memory spikes and we see a burst of evictions. attaching the sampled stats below.

maria: SAMPLE SNAPSHOT (12:43 UTC)
```
kv_resident_bytes=2483670016
kv_frag_percent=41
pages_swapped_to_disk=18
evictions_per_min=92
active_prefixes=3400
avg_prefix_len=120
last_compaction_age_seconds=320
```

maria: repro steps: run `perf/run_longctx_kv.sh --seed=82 --route=chat_stream` on canary; this is repeatable locally on my dev box and on canary GPU pool.

ashok: Ack. Any recent changes to key derivation or prefix hashing? that fragmentation number looks high.

liam: We merged the kernel-selection heuristics change yesterday (deploy 2026-03-12, sha: 0f9c1ab). It introduced a small change to the cache key salt that was intended to avoid cross-tenant collisions. Could be related.

maria: Good catch — I can correlate the timeline. The regression shows up immediately after that deploy. When I force old salt the resident drops to ~1.9GB and frag down to ~28%.

sophie: Interesting. Could be an interaction: new kernel picks prefer bigger batch windows which increases long-lived KV lifetimes, and the key salt change changed coalescing (prev keys collided more, so we got more reuse).

ashok: So two orthogonal effects: (1) batching/kernel change => longer-lived KV entries => higher steady-state. (2) keying change => reduced accidental reuse => higher unique prefixes => fragmentation. Together -> eviction surge.

liam: Agreed. I ran a quick diff of prefix counts: before=~2500 unique prefixes per route, after=~3400. That matches maria's active_prefixes value.

maria: Repro log excerpt from canary run (truncated):
```
[12:42:13] route=chat_stream seq=1 prefix=conv-491a2 hash=0x9f3a... alloc=48KB
[12:42:45] route=chat_stream seq=2 prefix=conv-3b2c1 hash=0x1a7b... alloc=112KB
[12:43:10] eviction: prefix=conv-2f11 age=298s freed=1.2MB
[12:43:14] paging kvmapped=3 pages swapped
[12:43:28] compaction started; scanned=4300 slots
```

sophie: Can we run targeted sampling where we pin batching/window to old behavior but keep new key salt, and vice versa? That would isolate.

maria: I'm running four matrix runs now: (A) old kernel + old salt, (B) old kernel + new salt, (C) new kernel + old salt, (D) new kernel + new salt. I'll post results in ~30m.

deploy-bot: deploy 0f9c1ab rolled to canary at 2026-03-12T04:10:23Z :white_check_mark:

ashok: FYI we should also dump the compaction heap histogram during the run (`/debug/kv/heap_hist`) — maybe fragmentation hotspots show a pattern (prefix length groups, tenant id distribution).

liam: Added a tiny profiler patch to sample prefix fingerprints every 5s; if results show spikes we can revert the salt change.

maria: MATRIX RESULTS (30m)
```
A: resident=1.92GB frag=27% evict/min=12
B: resident=2.05GB frag=34% evict/min=21
C: resident=2.12GB frag=29% evict/min=35
D: resident=2.48GB frag=41% evict/min=92
```

maria: So both changes contribute, but combined is worst. D is the current-prod canary.

sophie: That aligns with hypothesis. Action: rollback the key salt change on canary and re-run D config to confirm. If that helps, we'll roll back then iterate on kernel batching tuning separately.

ashok: I'm happy to take the rollback. Also adding a temporary guard in kernel-selection to avoid large batch windows for routes with avg ctx > 6k tokens.

liam: +1. Also make a note to add a regression test: longctx_kv_stability that asserts resident < 2.2GB on canary with 12k tokens and 95th p99 evictions threshold.

maria: I'll open an issue with the traces and attach the heap_hist dumps. TAGS: perf, kv-cache, regression, bake. Assigning to @ashok for rollback and @liam for test.

ashok: rolled back key-salt on canary at 12:55 UTC (rollback sha: 7b3e4d2). running the same longctx job now.

maria: post-rollback snapshot:
```
kv_resident_bytes=2013456896
kv_frag_percent=29
evictions_per_min=18
```

maria: that's within acceptable bounds. leaving canary on fallback kernel-window guard until we have a better batching heuristic.

sophie: Great. Next steps: (1) liam to add regression test + perf harness; (2) ashok to ship kernel window guard; (3) maria to surface telemetry for cross-tenant prefix dispersion.

liam: I'll PR the regression test this afternoon.

ashok: I'll follow-up with a short postmortem in #postmortems once we have final numbers.

maria: thanks all — surprised this compound interaction surfaced only in longctx runs, worth adding long-context smoke to our CI perf suite. :thumbsup:
